tip.title: How to study
tip.text: Learn the examples aloud, complete the quiz, then produce your own answer without copying the model.

sections.title: Core words and phrases
sections.description: Flip each card, listen, and create one personal example.

cards.definition: We need a loaf of bread.
I buy fresh vegetables every week.
Can I have a bottle of water?
She bought a packet of rice.
What is the price of this jacket?
We have enough milk for breakfast.

tip.title: Recall practice
tip.text: Cover the English term, read the Vietnamese meaning, and retrieve the full phrase from memory.

sections.title: Grammar bridge
sections.description: Master the structures that connect this A1 module to the next stage.

points.title: Countable nouns
points.function: Use a/an and plural forms with things you can count.
examples: How many eggs do we need?

points.title: Uncountable nouns
points.function: Use some, any and much with food such as rice or water.
examples: We do not have much time.

points.title: Polite requests
points.function: Use Can I have...? or I’d like... in shops and cafés.
examples: Can I have a coffee, please?

tip.title: Accuracy first
tip.text: Notice the verb form in every example, then change the subject or time expression to make a new sentence.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.description: Choose the best answer, then read the explanation.

questions.prompt: We need ___ apple for the salad.
questions.explanation: Apple begins with a vowel sound, so use an.

questions.prompt: Is there ___ cheese in the fridge?
questions.explanation: Use any in questions with uncountable nouns.
Oranges are countable, so use many. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.

questions.prompt: I would like two ___ of water.
questions.explanation: After two, use the plural bottles. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.

questions.prompt: This shirt is ten pounds. That is a good ___.
questions.explanation: A good price means the cost is reasonable.
After can, use the base verb have. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.

tip.title: Use the clue
tip.text: Look for time expressions, the subject, and words before or after the gap before choosing.

sections.title: Listening: Ordering Lunch
sections.description: Listen to a customer ordering food and identify prices and choices.

audio.transcript: Good afternoon. Can I have a chicken sandwich, please? Certainly. Would you like a drink with that? Yes, an orange juice, please. Anything else? How much is the chocolate cake? It's three pounds fifty. No cake, thank you. I'll have an apple instead. That's six pounds eighty altogether. Here you are. Thank you. Your sandwich will be ready in five minutes.

gistQuestions.explanation: They are ordering a sandwich and drink at a café.

detailQuestions.prompt: What drink does the customer choose?
detailQuestions.explanation: The customer asks for orange juice. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.
The server says the total is six pounds eighty.

tip.title: Listening Tip
tip.text: Prices often contain similar-sounding numbers. Listen to the whole amount before choosing.

sections.title: Build a spoken answer
sections.description: Answer each question aloud. Aim for a clear answer plus one reason or detail.
questions: What food do you buy every week?
Order a drink and a snack politely.
sections.sampleAnswer: I usually shop at a market near my home. I buy vegetables, eggs and some rice. In a café, I say: Can I have a tea and a sandwich, please?

tip.title: Speak in layers
tip.text: Start with a direct answer, add a reason, then give one example or detail.

sections.title: Independent writing
sections.description: Write a shopping message for a family member.

prompt.situation: List what you need, give quantities, and ask them to check one price.
prompt.referenceAnswer: I usually shop at a market near my home. I buy vegetables, eggs and some rice. In a café, I say: Can I have a tea and a sandwich, please?

tip.title: Final check
tip.text: Check verb forms, word order, spelling, and whether every sentence helps answer the task.
